question.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2},\,y=-t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =-2x,\,t=-y.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=-2x$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =-2x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${y}^{2}=-2x.$
